config.title: Cash-Only Restaurants in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Practical payment questions for bakery counters, market stalls and restaurant meals.

items.q: Are restaurants in Berlin cash only?
items.a: No. Card and contactless payments are widespread, but a venue can set its own payment policy. Smaller shops, markets and some restaurants may still prefer or require cash, so ask before you commit to an order.

items.q: How do I ask if I can pay by card in German?
items.a: Say "Kann ich mit Karte zahlen?" It means "Can I pay by card?" Ask at the bakery counter, while choosing at a market stall, or when you sit down for a restaurant meal.

items.q: How much cash should I carry for food in Berlin?
items.a: There is no universal amount. Keep only a modest backup that suits your budget and comfort, rather than treating cash as the only payment plan for a whole trip. Ask early if a particular venue accepts cards.

items.q: Should I find an ATM after I have ordered at a cash-only restaurant?
items.a: Avoid making that your default plan. Ask before ordering. If a venue is cash only and you do not have enough, decide before the meal whether a nearby ATM is practical or another restaurant is the better move.

items.q: Do Berlin market stalls accept cards?
items.a: It varies by stall and can change with the seller's setup. Do not assume one market stall accepts the same method as the next one. Ask while you are choosing what to buy.
